newsitem.title: ITALY: Minister, union see Italy metalworkers deal close.
newsitem.headline: Minister, union see Italy metalworkers deal close.

text.p: Labour Minister Tiziano Treu and an Italian trades union leader said on Wednesday they hoped a protracted pay dispute in the engineering and metalworking industry could be settled by the weekend.
"It is a hope that has some foundation," Treu told reporters in parliament. "A greater willingness to conclude has emerged on both sides compared with the recent days."
Treu said Prime Minister Romano Prodi would meet trades union leaders on Friday to discuss the dispute, which has been running since a contract agreement expired last June.
"If on Friday with the unions we see the possibility of white smoke (success), then we will call in the industrialists immediately to conclude in a couple of days at the most."
UIL leader Pietro Larizza, whose trades union is one of Italy's three main labour confederations, said there was a chance a reasonable settlement "could be found as soon as this weekend."
The government suggested in December that management give workers an average 200,000 lire per month pay increase.
Unions, which had been seeking a 230,000 lire increase, accepted the proposals, but the main industry group Federmeccanica has stuck to its original 139,000 lire offer.
Employers' groups say the government plan is inflationary. They are seeking a lower pay deal in underdeveloped southern Italy and tax breaks to lessen the impact of any accord.
The dispute, which involves some 1.7 million workers, is expected to set the tone for pay deals in a number of other Italian industrial sectors.
Unions in the industry have already staged three one-day stoppages to press their claims.
